body:
Pushed 1d17e32, fixes from an audit of this PR (each checked against the code):
- `VmmRange`: a run whose `cuMemSetAccess` failed stayed counted as mapped, so a later `map_range` skipped it and the chunks were never made accessible. It is unmapped and freed again now (`commit_run`).
- A failed growth or trim could leave `host_res`, `d_res` and the slot range half-changed while serve went on to the next request. Such a failure now stops the engine, as other CUDA failures do. The residency uploads are checked.
- The trim maps the chunks it takes back as one run (one `cuMemSetAccess` instead of one per 2 MiB chunk). It refills the slots with async copies and one sync instead of a blocking `cudaMemcpy` per expert.

IQ2_XS: the same served scenario (grow at a request and mid-decode, trim and refill, regrow, a parked conversation's restore) runs as before; `vmm_test` passes.

Rebased on 0.1.32 (c499bd1). One conflict, in `generate.cpp`, and both sides are kept:
- **Session start.** #340's `STRATA_SPLIT_SMALL_OWN` block stays, then `kvg_start`. The split block runs on a layer split only, and the elastic K/V is single-GPU (`!multi_gpu`), so they never act together.
- **A request's start.** #284's `wait_commit` comes first, then the K/V growth. Its quiesce synchronizes the device anyway.

Checked on 0.1.32: IQ2_XS (ISTA), RTX 5090, a fixed `--expert-cache`, `--vram-reserve-mib 1500`. The first generated token's logits (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`, now in main) are byte-identical to main's after a 2K and a 32K prompt. Every target builds with `STRATA_BUILD_TESTS`.

With `--kv-grow`, a cache budget below the free VRAM is needed for a byte-for-byte comparison:
- **Why.** `--expert-cache N` is a byte budget that the free VRAM caps. With `--kv-grow` the start leaves 3.1 GiB more free, so at `--expert-cache 14900` the cache gets 15,628 slots instead of main's 15,445. That is the point of the change, but then the first token is computed differently.
- **Check at `--expert-cache 13000`** (13,643 slots either way):
  - the logits are identical to main's;
  - the 256 greedy tokens are identical to main's;
  - the K/V stayed at 16,384 cells, with no growth needed.
- **At 32K** the K/V grew to 32,768 cells, and the cache gave 151 slots for it.

Tested on Windows 11 (WDDM): RTX 4080 SUPER 32 GB (sm_89), Ryzen 7 5800X3D, 64 GB, PCIe 3.0, CUDA 13.3; IQ3_S at `--max-context 262144`, int8 K/V, `--expert-cache auto` with `--expert-profile`, every expert in RAM (the arena is pinned in 47 slices, 45 of 46.8 GiB). `vmm_test` passes. Build: 0.1.32 (+#363, #413, #346) with this PR merged together with #385, #372, #374 and #407, no conflicts; `STRATA_KV_GROW=1` against unset in the same build.

- The auto sizing sees 24.85 instead of 21.76 GiB free: 12693 instead of 11055 slots (the K/V starts with 16384 cells, 0.25 of 3.35 GiB).
- Decode, 256-token requests, 3 per cell, ms per round / tokens per second:

| | greedy 8K | greedy 64K | sampled 8K | sampled 64K |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| unset | 21.4 / 124.6 | 21.7 / 127.3 | 20.7 / 118.2 | 21.8 / 130.5 |
| `STRATA_KV_GROW=1` | 20.4 / 132.0 | 21.6 / 128.3 | 20.6 / 123.9 | 21.7 / 129.4 |

  At 8K the CPU computes 0.52 instead of 0.92 experts per layer (VRAM hits 98.3 instead of 96.8 %). For the 64K requests the K/V grew once to 65536 cells (330 slots given up, 12363 still hold experts); there the VRAM hit rate was 98.3 % without it already, and nothing changes.
- Prefill: fresh 32K / 64K prompts +1.1 / +0.8 %. Short prompts gain more, as fewer experts have to be streamed: a 2K prompt takes 2.45 instead of 2.68 s, and the second, 923-token piece of the 64K prompt (read here as 63035 + 923 tokens) 1.76 instead of 1.92 s (about 800 instead of 985 ms waiting for copies).
- With the conversation cache (`--conversation-cache-mib 2816 --conversation-cache-slots 2`), a main agent (60K), subagents (15K) and a second main agent (100K) taking turns: the K/V grows before each restore (to 65536 cells for the 60K conversation, 106496 for the 100K one) and is trimmed when a 15K subagent takes over (330 / 601 slots back, refilled from the profile). Time to first token was never longer (back at the main agent 3.0 -> 2.8 s and 2.8 -> 2.6 s, the other steps equal or 0.1-0.2 s shorter); parked and restored sizes and RAM as without.
- As you wrote, the tokens differ: the deterministic requests diverge from token 30, since experts the CPU computed before now run on the GPU.
- No errors in 4 engine starts and 44 requests with it.

I run with it now: `STRATA_KV_GROW=1` in the config's `env`, so builds without this PR still start with the same config. Thanks!

Rebased on 0.1.37, plus a fix from a code review (7e5b7e7).

**The bug:** with `--kv-grow` the K/V is made elastic at session init and maps its first 16,384 cells. Growing it needs more than init checks: a device residency table, cache slots and a loan above the floor.
- Without them, `kvg_start` left the growth off and nothing mapped more. That happens with `--no-pool`, `--no-token-graph`, the dump modes, or `--expert-cache auto` resolving to 0.
- A prompt past 16K then wrote K/V into unmapped memory.
- Reproduced on IQ2_XS with `--kv-grow --no-token-graph` and a 32K prompt: `prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access was encountered`.

**Now:** such a run maps the whole window from new memory at start ("elastic K/V off for this run ... mapped up front"), or stops with a message if it does not fit. The same 32K prompt reads through: 32,036 tokens in 4 chunks.

The growth's and the trim's residency-table uploads also wait for their own copy. A pageable `cudaMemcpy` may return before its DMA lands, and the streams that read the table are non-blocking. The same pattern elsewhere is #550's subject.

Without `--kv-grow`, nothing changes.

We'd take `--kv-grow` as an opt-in. Please rebase it on 0.1.38. Without the flag, the output must stay byte-identical to 0.1.38 (fixed cache, 10/10).

I rebased this onto 0.1.38 (c053829). The only conflict was the source list in CMakeLists.txt (`peer_experts.cpp` beside `vmm.cpp`). `--kv-grow` stays opt-in, and nothing changes without it.

Without the flag, compared with v0.1.38 built from the tag with the same toolchain:

- **Setup:** RTX 5090, IQ2_XS, fixed `--expert-cache 14900`, `--max-context 262144 --kv int8 --spec 4`. Five prompts (two short chats of 24 and 44 tokens, then 2K, 8K and 16K documents), each run twice, interleaved with v0.1.38. Every pair compared byte for byte: the first-token logits (`STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS`) and 64 greedy tokens.
- **Result: 10/10 byte-identical**, logits and tokens both.
- **Decode** in the same runs:

| prompt | v0.1.38 | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| chat, 24 | 178.5 / 172.8 | 168.8 / 172.6 |
| chat, 44 | 149.7 / 149.5 | 147.0 / 149.4 |
| 2K | 164.5 / 164.6 | 165.4 / 164.3 |
| 8K | 174.1 / 173.7 | 173.9 / 174.1 |
| 16K | 182.8 / 183.2 | 183.5 / 182.8 |

Decode is in tokens/s, rounds 1 / 2. The one low cell, 168.8 on the 24-token chat, is run-to-run spread: the second round gives 172.6 against 172.8.

**With `--kv-grow`, on the same rebased build** (cache auto, a 32K document, 64 tokens):
- The run starts with 16,384 of 262,144 cells in VRAM.
- The expert cache holds 17,626 slots. With a fixed-size K/V it gets 15,342 at the same reserve (1500 MiB).
- For the prompt, the K/V grew to 32,768 cells (0.46 GiB). The cache gave 145 slots for it.
- Prefill ran at 6,783 tokens/s, then 64 tokens decoded at 185 tokens/s, with no errors.
